Menus and dialogs are built when opened and need nothing.
619:- A resumed conversation is replayed from its transcript (v89.0): `--resume` in print mode restores the agent's memory in full but emits none of the history — measured, the stream carries `system/init` and then the new turn, nothing else (the 55 K cache-creation tokens on the first request are the only sign the transcript was loaded). So resuming from Session History left the agent remembering everything while the chat opened blank, which is what "session history doesn't load in native mode" was. `TryReplayResumedTranscriptAsync` (NativeChat.cs) reads the same JSONL the Session History dialog reads — via `ResolveSessionDirectoryAsync`, so the WSL provider's `\\wsl.localhost\` path works unchanged — and renders user/assistant rows into the chat in place of the welcome card, reusing `ExtractUserText` and the dialog's text/thinking formatting (`AppendAssistantTextPart`) so both surfaces skip the tool-result rows the CLI re-injects as "user" messages identically. Parsing runs in `Task.Run` (a long session is megabytes) and returns plain data, since a view model may only be built on the UI thread. Tool calls (v241.0): until then the replay reused `ExtractAssistantText`, written for the plain-text View export, which flattens every `tool_use` to `[tool: Name]` — so a resumed chat showed that marker where the live chat had shown a card. Not a recorded decision: the replay (v89.0) shipped the same day as the tool cards (v87.0) and simply reused the export helper. `ReadResumedTranscript(TextReader, maxMessages, maxToolCards, maxSummaryLines)` (internal static, `Tests/ResumedTranscriptReplayTests.cs`) now emits user/assistant rows, a `ToolCall` row per `tool_use` (paired with its `tool_result` by `tool_use_id`, result truncated like a live one via `TruncateToolResult`, flattened via `ClaudeStreamParser.FlattenResultContent`) and summary rows; assistant text before and after a call stays on its own side of the card. `ResumedTranscriptBuilder` keeps two sliding windows while reading: `ResumedTranscriptMaxMessages` (1000 since v279.0; 200 before, a v89.0 judgement call) counts only user/assistant messages, and dropping the oldest message also drops the thinking before it and the tool and thinking rows that followed it, keeping only the thinking that leads straight into the next message (thinking can sit between tool calls), so the replay never opens on orphaned thinking or cards and the message count stays exact; within that, `ResumedTranscriptMaxToolCards` (200 since v279.0; 500 at first, lowered to 40 in v252.0, before the list was virtualized) keeps the newest calls as full cards and reduces older ones to `BuildToolSummaryLine` (`▤ Read · …\src\Foo.cs`, the card header's glyph/title/target), freeing their input and result. Each run of summarized calls between two messages becomes one `Notice` row capped at `ResumedToolSummaryMaxLines` (30, then "… and N more"), so the row count stays bounded by the message cap. Cards are built by `BuildReplayedToolCallMessage` through the same `BuildToolCallMessage` the live stream uses (default session and parallel tabs), finished (`IsRunning = false`) and collapsed — a failed call does not open itself as a live one does. Their diff is deferred: `ChatToolPresenter.Describe(..., includeDiff: false)` sets `DiffDeferred` instead of running DiffPlex, and `ChatMessageViewModel.SetDeferredDiff` builds it (and the `+N -M` badge, which comes from the diff) on the first `IsExpanded = true`. Without virtualization (`MessagesList` sits in a `StackPanel` inside the outer `ScrollViewer`, so every row is realized) the diff was the costly part of hundreds of cards. Thinking (v279.0): `thinking` parts become their own `Thinking` rows (`ResumedTranscriptBuilder.AddThinking`, not counted as messages), shown collapsed with the live row's caption, so the body is only rendered when opened; skipped between `a394bd4` and v278.0 because, before virtualization, rendering it inline stalled Visual Studio for ~30 s. The limits are a safety cap, not a performance knob: with the virtualized list (#219) the restore cost does not depend on them. A change to either limit must come with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` makes such a change visible in review. Codex replay is unchanged (text only, tool items dropped). The id is read in `TryStartNativeModeAsync` before `CreateAgentSession` consumes `_pendingResumeSessionId`, and passed in — `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` resumes through that same field for every model/effort/permission/plan change, and sourcing the replay from anywhere else would re-render the whole conversation on each one
620:- Codex history resume (v132.0; native empty-turn fallback v133.0): `OneShotSessionOptions.ResumeSessionId` seeds `OneShotResumeSession.SessionId`, so the very first user turn takes the already-existing `codex exec resume <thread-id>` branch; `StartAsync` emits that confirmed id immediately so saved titles/colors apply before a new turn. `TryReplayResumedTranscriptAsync` reads the same thread through App Server and renders user/agent messages (last 200) before the welcome card can appear. Some resumable native rollouts — especially interrupted or rolled-back threads — are listed with a preview and path while `thread/read {includeTurns:true}` returns an empty `turns` array. For those only, `CodexAppServerClient` falls back to the rollout's `event_msg` user/agent records (or user/assistant `response_item` records for older formats), excluding injected environment/permission/abort messages. The selected provider determines which App Server is launched, keeping Windows and WSL stores separate; Linux paths are never guessed or read through the native fallback
789:- Tab status glyph and automatic title (v259.0, `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.ChatTabStatus.cs`, pure parts in `UI/ChatTabStatus.cs` and `Agents/SessionTitleGenerator.cs`). VS does not draw a tool window's `BitmapImageMoniker` on a document tab, so the status goes into the caption text, the way Claude Code itself titles a terminal (✳ when idle): `ChatTabCaption.WithStatus` puts ⏳ working / ❓ waiting / ✳ done / ❌ error in front of `BuildChatTabCaption` (which shows the title alone once there is one). State lives in `NativeChatSessionState.TabStatus` (`_defaultTabStatus` for the default session); `SetChatTabStatus` is called at send (Working; Error when the send throws), `ShowNativeInteractionCore` and the permission dialog (WaitingForUser), `OnChatInteractionResolved` and the dialog's close (`ResumeWorkingChatTabStatus`, back to Working only while the turn is in flight), `CompleteNativeTurn*` (Done, unless an error was reported during the turn), and `SessionError` (Error). A resume relaunch settles a stale Working/WaitingForUser to Done (`SettleChatTabStatusAfterRelaunch`), since it ends the running turn without a `TurnCompleted`. Title: a tab with no custom title (and not a GitHub issue tab) takes `ChatTabCaption.TitleFromPrompt` of the first non-slash prompt at send time; with `AutoTitleChatTabsWithAi` and a Claude provider, `GenerateAiChatTitleAsync` then runs `RunClaudeOneShotAsync` (extracted from Recommend AI Model) with `GetSessionTitleArguments` (haiku, no tools/MCP/history) and replaces it. Since v289.0 the answer is forced into `SessionTitleGenerator.JsonSchema` (`structured_output.title`; the `result` text is only a fallback) and the call runs in the temp folder (`inWorkspace: false`), not the workspace: as plain text, with the project's CLAUDE.md loaded, haiku sometimes replied to the prompt ("Ano pane, zkusím to najít") instead of naming it. The prompt-based title is tab-scoped and in memory only. The AI title also names the session (v276.0), so Session History, the welcome card's recent list and the CLI's `/resume` show it: `GenerateAiChatTitleAsync` → `SaveAutoSessionName` writes it to `SessionCustomTitles` like a rename and appends the CLI title records (`KeepClaudeTitleInTranscriptAsync`). Only for a conversation the prompt opened (`IsNewConversation`: no reply and no earlier prompt in the transcript) — a resumed old session is not named after whatever is asked next; never over an existing name (re-checked when saving); and while the agent has no session id yet the title waits in `PendingSessionName` (`_defaultPendingSessionName`) and is saved by the `TurnCompleted` handlers. `KeepClaudeTitleInTranscriptAsync` also runs after every Claude native turn (`SyncClaudeTranscript`): the CLI picker reads only a transcript's head and last 64 KB, so a name written after the first turn would fall out of a long live session's tail — when the tail has no `custom-title` record, the saved name's pair is appended again (a no-op otherwise; a name given in the CLI mid-session and then pushed out of the tail would be overwritten by the saved one — accepted edge). `ResetChatTabTopic` clears the auto title (and the status) whenever another conversation starts in the tab — native start, a relaunch without resume, a history resume into a parallel tab — and the request token (`AutoTitleRequest`) makes a late AI answer for the old conversation a no-op.
794:- The welcome card is the extension's own startup banner (v88.0) — `ShowChatWelcome(workspace)` → `ChatTranscript.ShowWelcome(title, facts, tips)`. Native mode never sees the CLI's greeting: the agent runs headless and its banner is not part of the event stream, so an empty transcript said nothing about what was running. Shown from exactly two places — after `session.StartAsync` in `TryStartNativeModeAsync`, and at the end of `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` only when `forceNewSession`, since a model or permission switch keeps the conversation and a fresh-start card mid-thread would read as if it had been thrown away. It lives inside the scroll content above `MessagesList` (not layered over it, which would cover the first answer) and is dropped by `OnMessagesChanged` on the first `IsUser` row — not on the first row of any kind, or the "New chat" notice posted by the same relaunch would erase it immediately. `Clear()` hides it, leaving the caller to decide whether a new conversation is starting. Narrow tabs (v244.0): the left (mascot/facts) column stays `Auto` at its natural width; once the tips beside it would wrap so far that they are more than `WelcomeCardLayout.StackHeightRatio` (1.2) times as tall as that column is wide (`WelcomeCardLayout.ShouldStack`; the tips' height, not the card's — a tall left column is not helped by stacking), `ApplyWelcomeLayout` moves the tips into row 2 under a horizontal divider. With the recent list shown (below) the height test is skipped — the list stays beside the facts whatever its height, and only a column with no room at all (`TipsWidth <= 0`) still stacks. `RefreshWelcomeLayout` probes the *side-by-side* height — `Measure` of the left panel unconstrained and of the tips panel at `TipsWidth`, margins swapped for the side-by-side ones — never the current height: stacked, the tips are much shorter, so testing that would flip the card back and forth. Because the probe is hypothetical it is idempotent, so it runs on every `SizeChanged` (height too — zoom, new content) and the flip's own resize settles in one pass; it is deferred to `DispatcherPriority.Loaded` since it measures, and ends with `InvalidateMeasure` so the grid re-measures the probed panels with its real constraints. The "Signed in as Name (email)" fact is the longest line, so `ShowChatWelcome` passes it through `WelcomeCardLayout.BreakBeforeEmail`, which moves a trailing `(…@…)` onto its own line (the facts are plain `TextBlock`s, so `\n` is a line break); the transcript notice with the same text is left on one line. Recent conversations (v276.0): for a Claude provider `ShowChatWelcome` also calls `BeginWelcomeRecentSessionsLookup`, which reads the workspace's newest transcripts in the background (`LoadRecentClaudeSessionsAsync`: files by mtime, parsed only until `WelcomeRecentSessionCount` = 5 with at least one prompt are found; name = transcript title, else the saved one) and hands rows to `ChatTranscriptView.SetWelcomeRecentSessions`. With rows, the right column (`WelcomeTipsPanel`) shows `WelcomeRecentPanel` and folds the tips (`WelcomeTipsSection`) behind a "Show tips" link (`_welcomeTipsExpanded`, reset by `HideWelcome`, never saved); no rows or another agent → tips as before. The list survives `ShowWelcome` re-renders (version/account lookups); `_welcomeRecentLookups` stops those re-renders from starting parallel reads, and the result is applied only while the card is still visible. Since v276.0 sessions open in a chat tab are no longer skipped (the card then disagreed with Session History): `TryFindOpenChatTab` (matches `SessionId` or `ResumableSessionId` of `_agentSession` and every `_nativeSessions` entry) adds "already open" to the row, and a click on such a row brings that tab forward (`SwitchToOpenChatTabAsync`) instead of resuming the conversation a second time. The list is also re-read whenever the transcript becomes visible again with the card still up (`IsVisibleChanged` → `OnWelcomeTranscriptVisibleChanged`, workspace kept per transcript in `_welcomeRecentWorkspaces`) — before, it was read once and went stale while other tabs moved on. A row click raises `WelcomeSessionRequested` → `ResumeSessionAsync(info, owner tab)`, the same path as the History dialog; "All sessions…" raises `WelcomeAllSessionsRequested` → `ShowSessionHistoryDialogAsync`. Both are wired in the default and the per-tab composer wiring.
852:- Empty window: with no tab open, `UpdateEmptyState` shows `EmptyCard` — the chat welcome card's frame, caption and critter, centered — with buttons in the dialogs' rounded styles (`ThemedDialogStyles.xaml` merged into the view): "Start a new chat" raises `NewChatRequested` → `OnComposerNewChatRequested` with the selected transcript (none, so the main `ChatTranscript`) as sender; "Restore today's sessions" raises `ResumeTodayRequested` → `ResumeTodaysSessionsAsync` (SessionHistory.cs): the running/selected agent's history adapter lists the workspace, `TodaysSessionsToReopen` (shared with the Session History dialog's button of the same action) keeps today's conversations not already open, oldest first, confirmed above 5, each resumed with `ResumeSessionInNewTabAsync` (no seed tab, so settings defaults). The icon-only button beside it (`KnownMonikers.History`, tooltip "Session History") raises `SessionHistoryRequested` → `ShowSessionHistoryDialogAsync`, the same dialog as the composer's 🕘, with its search box. When nothing is subscribed to these events — VS restored the window before the Claude Code panel (which runs the chats) loaded — `ChatContainerToolWindow.Forward` opens the panel instead.

When the tab the dialog was opened from has a user prompt in its transcript (`ChatTabHasConversation`), `AskResumeInNewTab` asks New Tab (default button) / This Tab / Cancel; the question is asked with the history dialog as owner, so Cancel returns to the list. New Tab = `ResumeSessionInNewTabAsync` → `OpenResumedChatTabAsync` (ChatTabRestore.cs, the path that reopens tabs with the solution: deferred launch + transcript replay), seeded with the asking tab's model/effort/permission choices only when it runs the same agent, and carrying its `WorkspaceOverride`. This Tab keeps the old in-place `ResumeSessionAsync`. A tab with no user prompt resumes in place without asking, unless its composer holds a draft (`ChatTabHasDraft`: text, or attachments — `AttachedFiles` for a parallel tab, `attachedImagePaths` for the main chat): then it goes straight to New Tab, since a draft is usually a new topic and resuming over it hid what the user was writing. Terminal mode always resumes in place. Rows of conversations already open end with "· already open"
561:- Live switch: `Apply` raises `Loc.LanguageChanged`. `{local:Loc}` on a dependency property (templates and setters included) is a OneWay binding to the `LocSource` singleton, whose `Language` change re-runs `Loc.L` of the key — WPF listens weakly, so closed chats are not kept alive; elsewhere it stays the text translated at build time. Code that assigns such a property later replaces the binding and owns the text, so `RefreshChatLanguage()` (Settings dialog apply, settings backup load) redoes everything built in code — for the panel: `RefreshToolbarLayout()` (detach caption + the promoted buttons' tooltips, which the chat composers copy as plain text), the working-directory header, effort label, usage-bar labels/stale notice and last-prompt hint; then for the panel chat and every parallel session: `ChatTranscriptView.RefreshLanguage()` (placeholder, clear-button tooltip, modern Stop label, status/activity line, usage popup age, pending interaction cards via PropertyChanged), `UpdateChatComposerState` (selector captions, effort slider, usage ring), the welcome card while it is up, and the tab captions. Stored plain-text captions go through `Loc.Retranslate(shown)` — reverse map of the previous language's strings (first key wins on shared translations), then `L()` in the new one; formatted text is left as is until its next update. The modern/classic floating-button swap saves and restores the buttons' `Content` with `ReadLocalValue`/`RestoreLocalValue` so the binding survives. Messages already in the transcript (history, notices, resolved cards' outcome) keep the language they were written in. Live preview (v270.0): picking a language in the Settings combo calls `PreviewChatLanguage` at once — `Loc.SetLanguage` + `RefreshChatLanguage()` + `LocTree.Retranslate(dialog)` — so the panel, chats, tool windows and the dialog itself switch before OK; OK saves it, Cancel re-applies the saved language (`ApplyChatLanguage` + `RefreshChatLanguage`). `LocTree.Retranslate(root)` (LocExtension.cs) walks the logical tree of a window built in code and passes the window title, TextBlock/Run text and string Content/Header/ToolTip through `Loc.Retranslate`, skipping text boxes (user input) and data-bound properties (a local value would kill the `{local:Loc}` binding); ToolTips and ContextMenus are not logical children, so they are visited explicitly; formatted captions stay until the window is rebuilt. `RefreshChatLanguage()` also uses it for an open GitHub Issues window and redraws the attachment chips. `Loc.Apply` raises `LanguageChanged` listener by listener in try/catch, so one failing window cannot leave the rest in the old language (a throw used to escape into `ApplyChatLanguage`, whose catch fell back to English). The Code Changes and Claude Usage tool windows live outside the panel, so each subscribes to `Loc.LanguageChanged` itself: caption plus `DiffViewerControl.RefreshLanguage()` (re-runs `RefreshUI`, the auto-scroll tooltip and search results) / `ClaudeUsageControl.RefreshLanguage()` (last-checked line); they unsubscribe on close. Menus and dialogs are built when opened and need nothing.
619:- A resumed conversation is replayed from its transcript (v89.0): `--resume` in print mode restores the agent's memory in full but emits none of the history — measured, the stream carries `system/init` and then the new turn, nothing else (the 55 K cache-creation tokens on the first request are the only sign the transcript was loaded). So resuming from Session History left the agent remembering everything while the chat opened blank, which is what "session history doesn't load in native mode" was. `TryReplayResumedTranscriptAsync` (NativeChat.cs) reads the same JSONL the Session History dialog reads — via `ResolveSessionDirectoryAsync`, so the WSL provider's `\\wsl.localhost\` path works unchanged — and renders user/assistant rows into the chat in place of the welcome card, reusing `ExtractUserText` and the dialog's text/thinking formatting (`AppendAssistantTextPart`) so both surfaces skip the tool-result rows the CLI re-injects as "user" messages identically. Parsing runs in `Task.Run` (a long session is megabytes) and returns plain data, since a view model may only be built on the UI thread. Tool calls (v241.0): until then the replay reused `ExtractAssistantText`, written for the plain-text View export, which flattens every `tool_use` to `[tool: Name]` — so a resumed chat showed that marker where the live chat had shown a card. Not a recorded decision: the replay (v89.0) shipped the same day as the tool cards (v87.0) and simply reused the export helper. `ReadResumedTranscript(TextReader, maxMessages, maxToolCards, maxSummaryLines)` (internal static, `Tests/ResumedTranscriptReplayTests.cs`) now emits user/assistant rows, a `ToolCall` row per `tool_use` (paired with its `tool_result` by `tool_use_id`, result truncated like a live one via `TruncateToolResult`, flattened via `ClaudeStreamParser.FlattenResultContent`) and summary rows; assistant text before and after a call stays on its own side of the card. `ResumedTranscriptBuilder` keeps two sliding windows while reading: `ResumedTranscriptMaxMessages` (1000 since v279.0; 200 before, a v89.0 judgement call) counts only user/assistant messages, and dropping the oldest message also drops the thinking before it and the tool and thinking rows that followed it, keeping only the thinking that leads straight into the next message (thinking can sit between tool calls), so the replay never opens on orphaned thinking or cards and the message count stays exact; within that, `ResumedTranscriptMaxToolCards` (200 since v279.0; 500 at first, lowered to 40 in v252.0, before the list was virtualized) keeps the newest calls as full cards and reduces older ones to `BuildToolSummaryLine` (`▤ Read · …\src\Foo.cs`, the card header's glyph/title/target), freeing their input and result. Each run of summarized calls between two messages becomes one `Notice` row capped at `ResumedToolSummaryMaxLines` (30, then "… and N more"), so the row count stays bounded by the message cap. Cards are built by `BuildReplayedToolCallMessage` through the same `BuildToolCallMessage` the live stream uses (default session and parallel tabs), finished (`IsRunning = false`) and collapsed — a failed call does not open itself as a live one does. Their diff is deferred: `ChatToolPresenter.Describe(..., includeDiff: false)` sets `DiffDeferred` instead of running DiffPlex, and `ChatMessageViewModel.SetDeferredDiff` builds it (and the `+N -M` badge, which comes from the diff) on the first `IsExpanded = true`. Without virtualization (`MessagesList` sits in a `StackPanel` inside the outer `ScrollViewer`, so every row is realized) the diff was the costly part of hundreds of cards. Thinking (v279.0): `thinking` parts become their own `Thinking` rows (`ResumedTranscriptBuilder.AddThinking`, not counted as messages), shown collapsed with the live row's caption, so the body is only rendered when opened; skipped between `a394bd4` and v278.0 because, before virtualization, rendering it inline stalled Visual Studio for ~30 s. The limits are a safety cap, not a performance knob: with the virtualized list (#219) the restore cost does not depend on them. A change to either limit must come with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` makes such a change visible in review. Codex replay is unchanged (text only, tool items dropped). The id is read in `TryStartNativeModeAsync` before `CreateAgentSession` consumes `_pendingResumeSessionId`, and passed in — `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` resumes through that same field for every model/effort/permission/plan change, and sourcing the replay from anywhere else would re-render the whole conversation on each one
620:- Codex history resume (v132.0; native empty-turn fallback v133.0): `OneShotSessionOptions.ResumeSessionId` seeds `OneShotResumeSession.SessionId`, so the very first user turn takes the already-existing `codex exec resume <thread-id>` branch; `StartAsync` emits that confirmed id immediately so saved titles/colors apply before a new turn. `TryReplayResumedTranscriptAsync` reads the same thread through App Server and renders user/agent messages (last 200) before the welcome card can appear. Some resumable native rollouts — especially interrupted or rolled-back threads — are listed with a preview and path while `thread/read {includeTurns:true}` returns an empty `turns` array. For those only, `CodexAppServerClient` falls back to the rollout's `event_msg` user/agent records (or user/assistant `response_item` records for older formats), excluding injected environment/permission/abort messages. The selected provider determines which App Server is launched, keeping Windows and WSL stores separate; Linux paths are never guessed or read through the native fallback
789:- Tab status glyph and automatic title (v259.0, `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.ChatTabStatus.cs`, pure parts in `UI/ChatTabStatus.cs` and `Agents/SessionTitleGenerator.cs`). VS does not draw a tool window's `BitmapImageMoniker` on a document tab, so the status goes into the caption text, the way Claude Code itself titles a terminal (✳ when idle): `ChatTabCaption.WithStatus` puts ⏳ working / ❓ waiting / ✳ done / ❌ error in front of `BuildChatTabCaption` (which shows the title alone once there is one). State lives in `NativeChatSessionState.TabStatus` (`_defaultTabStatus` for the default session); `SetChatTabStatus` is called at send (Working; Error when the send throws), `ShowNativeInteractionCore` and the permission dialog (WaitingForUser), `OnChatInteractionResolved` and the dialog's close (`ResumeWorkingChatTabStatus`, back to Working only while the turn is in flight), `CompleteNativeTurn*` (Done, unless an error was reported during the turn), and `SessionError` (Error). A resume relaunch settles a stale Working/WaitingForUser to Done (`SettleChatTabStatusAfterRelaunch`), since it ends the running turn without a `TurnCompleted`. Since v289.0 the answer is forced into `SessionTitleGenerator.JsonSchema` (`structured_output.title`; the `result` text is only a fallback) and the call runs in the temp folder (`inWorkspace: false`), not the workspace: as plain text, with the project's CLAUDE.md loaded, haiku sometimes replied to the prompt ("Ano pane, zkusím to najít") instead of naming it. The prompt-based title is tab-scoped and in memory only. The AI title also names the session (v276.0), so Session History, the welcome card's recent list and the CLI's `/resume` show it: `GenerateAiChatTitleAsync` → `SaveAutoSessionName` writes it to `SessionCustomTitles` like a rename and appends the CLI title records (`KeepClaudeTitleInTranscriptAsync`). Only for a conversation the prompt opened (`IsNewConversation`: no reply and no earlier prompt in the transcript) — a resumed old session is not named after whatever is asked next; never over an existing name (re-checked when saving); and while the agent has no session id yet the title waits in `PendingSessionName` (`_defaultPendingSessionName`) and is saved by the `TurnCompleted` handlers. `KeepClaudeTitleInTranscriptAsync` also runs after every Claude native turn (`SyncClaudeTranscript`): the CLI picker reads only a transcript's head and last 64 KB, so a name written after the first turn would fall out of a long live session's tail — when the tail has no `custom-title` record, the saved name's pair is appended again (a no-op otherwise; a name given in the CLI mid-session and then pushed out of the tail would be overwritten by the saved one — accepted edge). `ResetChatTabTopic` clears the auto title (and the status) whenever another conversation starts in the tab — native start, a relaunch without resume, a history resume into a parallel tab — and the request token (`AutoTitleRequest`) makes a late AI answer for the old conversation a no-op.
794:- The welcome card is the extension's own startup banner (v88.0) — `ShowChatWelcome(workspace)` → `ChatTranscript.ShowWelcome(title, facts, tips)`. Native mode never sees the CLI's greeting: the agent runs headless and its banner is not part of the event stream, so an empty transcript said nothing about what was running. Shown from exactly two places — after `session.StartAsync` in `TryStartNativeModeAsync`, and at the end of `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` only when `forceNewSession`, since a model or permission switch keeps the conversation and a fresh-start card mid-thread would read as if it had been thrown away. With the recent list shown (below) the height test is skipped — the list stays beside the facts whatever its height, and only a column with no room at all (`TipsWidth <= 0`) still stacks. `RefreshWelcomeLayout` probes the *side-by-side* height — `Measure` of the left panel unconstrained and of the tips panel at `TipsWidth`, margins swapped for the side-by-side ones — never the current height: stacked, the tips are much shorter, so testing that would flip the card back and forth. Because the probe is hypothetical it is idempotent, so it runs on every `SizeChanged` (height too — zoom, new content) and the flip's own resize settles in one pass; it is deferred to `DispatcherPriority.Loaded` since it measures, and ends with `InvalidateMeasure` so the grid re-measures the probed panels with its real constraints. The "Signed in as Name (email)" fact is the longest line, so `ShowChatWelcome` passes it through `WelcomeCardLayout.BreakBeforeEmail`, which moves a trailing `(…@…)` onto its own line (the facts are plain `TextBlock`s, so `\n` is a line break); the transcript notice with the same text is left on one line. With rows, the right column (`WelcomeTipsPanel`) shows `WelcomeRecentPanel` and folds the tips (`WelcomeTipsSection`) behind a "Show tips" link (`_welcomeTipsExpanded`, reset by `HideWelcome`, never saved); no rows or another agent → tips as before. The list survives `ShowWelcome` re-renders (version/account lookups); `_welcomeRecentLookups` stops those re-renders from starting parallel reads, and the result is applied only while the card is still visible. Since v276.0 sessions open in a chat tab are no longer skipped (the card then disagreed with Session History): `TryFindOpenChatTab` (matches `SessionId` or `ResumableSessionId` of `_agentSession` and every `_nativeSessions` entry) adds "already open" to the row, and a click on such a row brings that tab forward (`SwitchToOpenChatTabAsync`) instead of resuming the conversation a second time. A row click raises `WelcomeSessionRequested` → `ResumeSessionAsync(info, owner tab)`, the same path as the History dialog; "All sessions…" raises `WelcomeAllSessionsRequested` → `ShowSessionHistoryDialogAsync`. Both are wired in the default and the per-tab composer wiring.
852:- Empty window: with no tab open, `UpdateEmptyState` shows `EmptyCard` — the chat welcome card's frame, caption and critter, centered — with buttons in the dialogs' rounded styles (`ThemedDialogStyles.xaml` merged into the view): "Start a new chat" raises `NewChatRequested` → `OnComposerNewChatRequested` with the selected transcript (none, so the main `ChatTranscript`) as sender; "Restore today's sessions" raises `ResumeTodayRequested` → `ResumeTodaysSessionsAsync` (SessionHistory.cs): the running/selected agent's history adapter lists the workspace, `TodaysSessionsToReopen` (shared with the Session History dialog's button of the same action) keeps today's conversations not already open, oldest first, confirmed above 5, each resumed with `ResumeSessionInNewTabAsync` (no seed tab, so settings defaults). The icon-only button beside it (`KnownMonikers.History`, tooltip "Session History") raises `SessionHistoryRequested` → `ShowSessionHistoryDialogAsync`, the same dialog as the composer's 🕘, with its search box. The list survives `ShowWelcome` re-renders (version/account lookups); `_welcomeRecentLookups` stops those re-renders from starting parallel reads, and the result is applied only while the card is still visible. Since v276.0 sessions open in a chat tab are no longer skipped (the card then disagreed with Session History): `TryFindOpenChatTab` (matches `SessionId` or `ResumableSessionId` of `_agentSession` and every `_nativeSessions` entry) adds "already open" to the row, and a click on such a row brings that tab forward (`SwitchToOpenChatTabAsync`) instead of resuming the conversation a second time. The list is also re-read whenever the transcript becomes visible again with the card still up (`IsVisibleChanged` → `OnWelcomeTranscriptVisibleChanged`, workspace kept per transcript in `_welcomeRecentWorkspaces`) — before, it was read once and went stale while other tabs moved on. A row click raises `WelcomeSessionRequested` → `ResumeSessionAsync(info, owner tab)`, the same path as the History dialog; "All sessions…" raises `WelcomeAllSessionsRequested` → `ShowSessionHistoryDialogAsync`. Both are wired in the default and the per-tab composer wiring.

+- The welcome card is the extension's own startup banner (v88.0) — `ShowChatWelcome(workspace)` → `ChatTranscript.ShowWelcome(title, facts, tips)`. Native mode never sees the CLI's greeting: the agent runs headless and its banner is not part of the event stream, so an empty transcript said nothing about what was running. Shown from exactly two places — after `session.StartAsync` in `TryStartNativeModeAsync`, and at the end of `RelaunchNativeSessionAsync` only when `forceNewSession`, since a model or permission switch keeps the conversation and a fresh-start card mid-thread would read as if it had been thrown away. It sits above `MessagesList` (not layered over it, which would cover the first answer) in its own `WelcomeScroll` ScrollViewer whose `MaxHeight` is bound to `TranscriptArea.ActualHeight` (v294.0): the `Auto` row measures the card with unlimited height, so a card taller than the tab (recent list + expanded tips) was cut off with no way to scroll and is dropped by `OnMessagesChanged` on the first `IsUser` row — not on the first row of any kind, or the "New chat" notice posted by the same relaunch would erase it immediately. `Clear()` hides it, leaving the caller to decide whether a new conversation is starting. Narrow tabs (v244.0): the left (mascot/facts) column stays `Auto` at its natural width; once the tips beside it would wrap so far that they are more than `WelcomeCardLayout.StackHeightRatio` (1.2) times as tall as that column is wide (`WelcomeCardLayout.ShouldStack`; the tips' height, not the card's — a tall left column is not helped by stacking), `ApplyWelcomeLayout` moves the tips into row 2 under a horizontal divider. With the recent list shown (below) the height test is skipped — the list stays beside the facts whatever its height, and only a column with no room at all (`TipsWidth <= 0`) still stacks. `RefreshWelcomeLayout` probes the *side-by-side* height — `Measure` of the left panel unconstrained and of the tips panel at `TipsWidth`, margins swapped for the side-by-side ones — never the current height: stacked, the tips are much shorter, so testing that would flip the card back and forth. Because the probe is hypothetical it is idempotent, so it runs on every `SizeChanged` (height too — zoom, new content) and the flip's own resize settles in one pass; it is deferred to `DispatcherPriority.Loaded` since it measures, and ends with `InvalidateMeasure` so the grid re-measures the probed panels with its real constraints. The "Signed in as Name (email)" fact is the longest line, so `ShowChatWelcome` passes it through `WelcomeCardLayout.BreakBeforeEmail`, which moves a trailing `(…@…)` onto its own line (the facts are plain `TextBlock`s, so `\n` is a line break); the transcript notice with the same text is left on one line. Recent conversations (v276.0): for a Claude provider `ShowChatWelcome` also calls `BeginWelcomeRecentSessionsLookup`, which reads the workspace's newest transcripts in the background (`LoadRecentClaudeSessionsAsync`: files by mtime, parsed only until `WelcomeRecentSessionCount` = 5 with at least one prompt are found; name = transcript title, else the saved one) and hands rows to `ChatTranscriptView.SetWelcomeRecentSessions`. With rows, the right column (`WelcomeTipsPanel`) shows `WelcomeRecentPanel` and folds the tips (`WelcomeTipsSection`) behind a "Show tips" link (`_welcomeTipsExpanded`, reset by `HideWelcome`, never saved); no rows or another agent → tips as before. The list survives `ShowWelcome` re-renders (version/account lookups); `_welcomeRecentLookups` stops those re-renders from starting parallel reads, and the result is applied only while the card is still visible. Since v276.0 sessions open in a chat tab are no longer skipped (the card then disagreed with Session History): `TryFindOpenChatTab` (matches `SessionId` or `ResumableSessionId` of `_agentSession` and every `_nativeSessions` entry) adds "already open" to the row, and a click on such a row brings that tab forward (`SwitchToOpenChatTabAsync`) instead of resuming the conversation a second time. The list is also re-read whenever the transcript becomes visible again with the card still up (`IsVisibleChanged` → `OnWelcomeTranscriptVisibleChanged`, workspace kept per transcript in `_welcomeRecentWorkspaces`) — before, it was read once and went stale while other tabs moved on. A row click raises `WelcomeSessionRequested` → `ResumeSessionAsync(info, owner tab)`, the same path as the History dialog; "All sessions…" raises `WelcomeAllSessionsRequested` → `ShowSessionHistoryDialogAsync`. Both are wired in the default and the per-tab composer wiring.

- The CLI version is probed in the background, never awaited. `BeginCliVersionLookup` runs `<cli> --version` (WSL: `wsl.exe bash -lic "<cli> --version"`, a login shell for the same reason the session launch uses one) with the executable resolved exactly as the launch resolves it, so the number shown is the one actually running. Results are cached in a static `ConcurrentDictionary<AiProvider, string>` where an empty value means "asked and got nothing" — that is what stops a missing or slow CLI from being probed again on every new chat. Both pipes are read asynchronously with `BeginOutputReadLine`/`BeginErrorReadLine` and the process is killed after 5 s: `StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()` on a CLI that never exits would strand a pool thread forever. The redraw is guarded by `ChatTranscript.IsWelcomeVisible` and a provider re-check, so a late answer cannot resurrect a card the first prompt already dismissed. `ExtractVersion` regexes the first version-shaped token out of the output because the CLIs disagree on the format (`2.1.220`, `codex-cli 0.5.0`, …).

- Facts and tips claim only what the chat can actually do. Model and effort are listed only for the agents whose choice the extension owns (the same condition as `SetSelectorAvailability`), and the tips cover ↑-history, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Scroll, the selectors and ✚ — deliberately *not* `@`-mentions or slash commands, which the composer does not implement. The mascot is drawn as `Rectangle`s in a `Viewbox` rather than typed as an emoji or a glyph: a missing font renders as an empty box, and its eyes are punched out in `ToolWindowBackgroundKey` so it reads the same under both themes.

- Provider switches are not resumable by definition (no two agents share a transcript), so they go through `RestartTerminalWithSelectedProviderAsync()`, which tears native mode down and starts it again — closing and reopening the tab on the way. `UpdateProviderSelection()` must run again *after* that call (v94.0): the pre-switch refresh still reads the outgoing agent off `_currentRunningProvider` (per the *Active provider UI rule*), so without the second call the tool-window caption kept the old provider name for the rest of the session.

256	## Add a new setting
257	
258	1. `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs` — add the property to the settings class with its default.
259	   Defaults must match what a fresh install should do; the JSON is merged over them.
260	2. Surface it — `ClaudeCodeControl.SettingsDialog.cs` (pick the right tab) or the ⚙ menu.
261	3. Apply it on load in `ClaudeCodeControl.Settings.cs` (`LoadSettings()` re-runs, so make the
262	   apply idempotent).
263	4. `ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Data Models & Settings* — add it to the Key settings list with its
264	   default and a one-line description.
265	
266	Persistence is JSON at `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\claudecode-settings.json` via
267	Newtonsoft.Json. Note that `SaveSettings()` deliberately preserves provider/model/effort fields
268	from disk during normal operation so parallel VS instances don't clobber each other — if your
269	setting is per-instance selection state, follow that pattern.
270	
271	---
272	
273	## Add a new UI file
274	
275	**XAML control** — both files go in `UI/`, and the csproj needs two entries:
276	
277	```xml
278	<Page Include="UI\Foo.xaml">
279	  <Generator>MSBuild:Compile</Generator>
280	  <SubType>Designer</SubType>
281	</Page>
282	...
283	<Compile Include="UI\Foo.xaml.cs">
284	  <DependentUpon>Foo.xaml</DependentUpon>
285	</Compile>
286	```
287	
288	**Partial class of `ClaudeCodeControl`** — goes in `Controls/`, named
289	`ClaudeCodeControl.<Area>.cs`, plus a plain `<Compile Include="...">` entry.
290	
291	Every `.cs` file needs the copyright header:
292	
293	```csharp
294	/* ***********************
295	 * Application: ClaudeCodeExtension
296	 * Autor:  Daniel Carvalho Liedke / Claude Code
297	 * Copyright © Daniel Carvalho Liedke 2026
298	 * Usage and reproduction in any manner whatsoever without the written permission of Daniel Carvalho Liedke is strictly forbidden.
299	 * Purpose: <description>
300	 * ***********************/
301	```
302	
303	Namespaces: `ClaudeCodeVS` for controls/models, `ClaudeCodeExtension` for the package.
304	
305	---
306	
307	## Localize chat text
308	
309	Scope (v270.0): the whole extension — chat tab, panel, menus, toolbar, Settings and other dialogs,
310	message boxes, the Code Changes and Claude Usage windows. Model names, effort levels and provider
311	names stay as the CLIs spell them.
312	
313	1. Write the English text wrapped: `L("Turn interrupted.")`, `L("Done in {0}", d)` (formats with
314	   the chat language's culture), XAML `{local:Loc 'Jump to the latest message'}` (escape `'` as `\'`).
315	   Static lists translated when shown: mark entries `N("...")`, call `L(entry)` at display time.
316	   Needs `using static ClaudeCodeVS.UI.Loc;`.
317	2. Never wrap text sent to the agent/CLI, slash commands, tool/provider/model names, log text or
318	   strings the code compares.
319	3. Translate it in **every** `lang/*.json` (19 files) in the same change — new, reworded or removed
320	   text alike. Keep the `{n}` placeholders, any leading/trailing space and a leading icon (`🤖 `,
321	   `■ `). `test.cmd` fails on a string missing from any file, on a translation whose English is gone
322	   from the code, on duplicate keys, empty values and on those three rules.
323	4. New built-in language: add it to `Loc.BuiltInLanguages` (code = .NET culture name, display name in
324	   that language), add `lang/<code>.json` with every key and an `<EmbeddedResource>` line in the
325	   csproj next to the others; the tests check the three agree. For a local fix or an extra language
326	   without a rebuild, drop the file in `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\lang` (it also
327	   overrides embedded entries).
328	5. Text set from code after the XAML is built does not follow a language switch on its own: make
329	   sure `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or the view's `RefreshLanguage()`) redoes it. A tool window that
330	   lives outside the panel subscribes to `Loc.LanguageChanged` itself (Code Changes, Claude Usage).
331	   A modeless window built in code is retranslated in place with `UI.LocTree.Retranslate(window)`
332	   from `RefreshChatLanguage()` (GitHub Issues). Modal dialogs and menus built when opened need nothing.
333

## Add a new setting

1. `Models/ClaudeCodeModels.cs` — add the property to the settings class with its default.
   Defaults must match what a fresh install should do; the JSON is merged over them.
2. Surface it — `ClaudeCodeControl.SettingsDialog.cs` (pick the right tab) or the ⚙ menu.
3. Apply it on load in `ClaudeCodeControl.Settings.cs` (`LoadSettings()` re-runs, so make the
   apply idempotent).
4. `ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Data Models & Settings* — add it to the Key settings list with its
   default and a one-line description.

Persistence is JSON at `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\claudecode-settings.json` via
Newtonsoft.Json. Note that `SaveSettings()` deliberately preserves provider/model/effort fields
from disk during normal operation so parallel VS instances don't clobber each other — if your
setting is per-instance selection state, follow that pattern.

---

## Add a new UI file

**XAML control** — both files go in `UI/`, and the csproj needs two entries:

```xml
<Page Include="UI\Foo.xaml">
  <Generator>MSBuild:Compile</Generator>
  <SubType>Designer</SubType>
</Page>

```

**Partial class of `ClaudeCodeControl`** — goes in `Controls/`, named
`ClaudeCodeControl.<Area>.cs`, plus a plain `<Compile Include="...">` entry.

Every `.cs` file needs the copyright header:

```csharp
/* ***********************
 * Application: ClaudeCodeExtension
 * Autor:  Daniel Carvalho Liedke / Claude Code
 * Copyright © Daniel Carvalho Liedke 2026
 * Usage and reproduction in any manner whatsoever without the written permission of Daniel Carvalho Liedke is strictly forbidden.
 * Purpose: <description>
 * ***********************/
```

Namespaces: `ClaudeCodeVS` for controls/models, `ClaudeCodeExtension` for the package.

---

## Localize chat text

Scope (v270.0): the whole extension — chat tab, panel, menus, toolbar, Settings and other dialogs,
message boxes, the Code Changes and Claude Usage windows. Model names, effort levels and provider
names stay as the CLIs spell them.

1. Write the English text wrapped: `L("Turn interrupted.")`, `L("Done in {0}", d)` (formats with
   the chat language's culture), XAML `{local:Loc 'Jump to the latest message'}` (escape `'` as `\'`).
   Static lists translated when shown: mark entries `N("...")`, call `L(entry)` at display time.
   Needs `using static ClaudeCodeVS.UI.Loc;`.
2. Never wrap text sent to the agent/CLI, slash commands, tool/provider/model names, log text or
   strings the code compares.
3. Translate it in **every** `lang/*.json` (19 files) in the same change — new, reworded or removed
   text alike. Keep the `{n}` placeholders, any leading/trailing space and a leading icon (`🤖 `,
   `■ `). `test.cmd` fails on a string missing from any file, on a translation whose English is gone
   from the code, on duplicate keys, empty values and on those three rules.
4. New built-in language: add it to `Loc.BuiltInLanguages` (code = .NET culture name, display name in
   that language), add `lang/<code>.json` with every key and an `<EmbeddedResource>` line in the
   csproj next to the others; the tests check the three agree. For a local fix or an extra language
   without a rebuild, drop the file in `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\lang` (it also
   overrides embedded entries).
5. Text set from code after the XAML is built does not follow a language switch on its own: make
   sure `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or the view's `RefreshLanguage()`) redoes it. A tool window that
   lives outside the panel subscribes to `Loc.LanguageChanged` itself (Code Changes, Claude Usage).
   A modeless window built in code is retranslated in place with `UI.LocTree.Retranslate(window)`
   from `RefreshChatLanguage()` (GitHub Issues). Modal dialogs and menus built when opened need nothing.

import json, io, sys
K = ["Search settings…",
     "Finds a setting in any tab by its name, its description or its choices. Ctrl+F jumps here, Esc clears the search.",
     "No setting matches the search."]
T = {
"pt-BR": ["Pesquisar configurações…", "Encontra uma configuração em qualquer aba pelo nome, pela descrição ou pelas opções. Ctrl+F vem para cá, Esc limpa a pesquisa.", "Nenhuma configuração corresponde à pesquisa."],
"es": ["Buscar configuración…", "Encuentra una opción en cualquier pestaña por su nombre, su descripción o sus valores. Ctrl+F lleva aquí, Esc borra la búsqueda.", "Ninguna opción coincide con la búsqueda."],
"fr": ["Rechercher un paramètre…", "Trouve un paramètre dans n'importe quel onglet par son nom, sa description ou ses choix. Ctrl+F vient ici, Échap efface la recherche.", "Aucun paramètre ne correspond à la recherche."],
"de": ["Einstellungen durchsuchen…", "Findet eine Einstellung auf jeder Registerkarte nach Name, Beschreibung oder Auswahlmöglichkeiten. Strg+F springt hierher, Esc leert die Suche.", "Keine Einstellung passt zur Suche."],
"it": ["Cerca impostazioni…", "Trova un'impostazione in qualsiasi scheda dal nome, dalla descrizione o dalle opzioni. Ctrl+F porta qui, Esc cancella la ricerca.", "Nessuna impostazione corrisponde alla ricerca."],
"nl": ["Instellingen zoeken…", "Vindt een instelling op elk tabblad op naam, beschrijving of keuzes. Ctrl+F springt hierheen, Esc wist de zoekopdracht.", "Geen instelling komt overeen met de zoekopdracht."],
"pl": ["Szukaj ustawień…", "Znajduje ustawienie na dowolnej karcie po nazwie, opisie lub opcjach. Ctrl+F przenosi tutaj, Esc czyści wyszukiwanie.", "Żadne ustawienie nie pasuje do wyszukiwania."],
"ru": ["Поиск настроек…", "Находит настройку на любой вкладке по названию, описанию или вариантам. Ctrl+F переходит сюда, Esc очищает поиск.", "Нет настроек, соответствующих поиску."],
"uk": ["Пошук налаштувань…", "Знаходить налаштування на будь-якій вкладці за назвою, описом або варіантами. Ctrl+F переходить сюди, Esc очищає пошук.", "Немає налаштувань, що відповідають пошуку."],
"tr": ["Ayarlarda ara…", "Herhangi bir sekmedeki ayarı adına, açıklamasına veya seçeneklerine göre bulur. Ctrl+F buraya gelir, Esc aramayı temizler.", "Aramayla eşleşen ayar yok."],
"ar": ["البحث في الإعدادات…", "يعثر على إعداد في أي علامة تبويب حسب اسمه أو وصفه أو خياراته. Ctrl+F ينقلك إلى هنا، وEsc يمسح البحث.", "لا يوجد إعداد يطابق البحث."],
"hi": ["सेटिंग खोजें…", "किसी भी टैब में सेटिंग को उसके नाम, विवरण या विकल्पों से ढूँढता है। Ctrl+F यहाँ लाता है, Esc खोज साफ़ करता है।", "खोज से कोई सेटिंग मेल नहीं खाती।"],
"id": ["Cari pengaturan…", "Menemukan pengaturan di tab mana pun berdasarkan nama, deskripsi, atau pilihannya. Ctrl+F menuju ke sini, Esc menghapus pencarian.", "Tidak ada pengaturan yang cocok dengan pencarian."],
"vi": ["Tìm cài đặt…", "Tìm một cài đặt trong bất kỳ thẻ nào theo tên, mô tả hoặc các lựa chọn của nó. Ctrl+F chuyển đến đây, Esc xóa tìm kiếm.", "Không có cài đặt nào khớp với tìm kiếm."],
"th": ["ค้นหาการตั้งค่า…", "ค้นหาการตั้งค่าในทุกแท็บจากชื่อ คำอธิบาย หรือตัวเลือก Ctrl+F เพื่อมาที่นี่ Esc เพื่อล้างการค้นหา", "ไม่มีการตั้งค่าที่ตรงกับการค้นหา"],
"ja": ["設定を検索…", "名前、説明、選択肢から任意のタブの設定を見つけます。Ctrl+F でここに移動し、Esc で検索をクリアします。", "検索に一致する設定はありません。"],
"ko": ["설정 검색…", "이름, 설명 또는 선택 항목으로 모든 탭의 설정을 찾습니다. Ctrl+F로 여기로 이동하고 Esc로 검색을 지웁니다.", "검색과 일치하는 설정이 없습니다."],
"zh-Hans": ["搜索设置…", "按名称、说明或选项在任意选项卡中查找设置。Ctrl+F 跳到这里，Esc 清除搜索。", "没有与搜索匹配的设置。"],
"zh-Hant": ["搜尋設定…", "依名稱、說明或選項在任何索引標籤中尋找設定。Ctrl+F 跳到這裡，Esc 清除搜尋。", "沒有符合搜尋的設定。"],
}
for code, vals in T.items():
    p = "lang/%s.json" % code
    s = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8", newline="").read()
    d = json.loads(s)
    nl = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in s else "\n"
    body = s.rstrip()
    assert body.endswith("}")
    body = body[:-1].rstrip()
    lines = []
    for k, v in zip(K, vals):
        assert k not in d, (code, k)
        lines.append("  " + json.dumps(k, ensure_ascii=False) + ": " + json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False))
    out = body + "," + nl + ("," + nl).join(lines) + nl + "}" + nl
    json.loads(out)
    io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(out)
print("ok", len(T))

The tab has its own message box with image paste and file attachments, plus agent, model, effort and permission selectors you can change mid-conversation. Turn off via *⚙ → Settings... → Terminal* to use the embedded terminal instead; Reasonix and any agent that can't run this way keep using the terminal.
21:- **Multi-line prompts** — Press **Enter** to send, **Shift+Enter** or **Ctrl+Enter** for a new line. To send with Ctrl+Enter instead, or to use a Send button, change the send key in *⚙ → Settings... → Prompt*.
25:- **Editor selection → prompt** — Click 📋 or right-click selected code → *Send Selection to Claude Code* to insert a formatted snippet (file path + line numbers + syntax-highlighted code fence) into the prompt. Turn on *Send selection as reference only* in *⚙ → Settings... → Prompt* to insert just the file path and line numbers.
41:- **On Agent Finish** — Optionally play a sound, show a notification (with duration, plus token count for Claude Code), and run an action (build/rebuild, run, tests, a script, or a follow-up command) when the agent goes idle. Configured per solution. Configure via *⚙ → Settings...*.
43:- **Pull before sending** — Runs `git pull` in the solution’s repository before your first prompt, so the agent never edits a file that is already out of date on the remote. Conflicts from that pull are handed to the agent to resolve. On by default; turn it off via *⚙ → Settings... → Automation*.
45:- **TFVC checkout** — In TFVC-bound solutions, Claude Code in native mode has read-only files checked out through Visual Studio before it edits them. On by default; turn it off via *⚙ → Settings... → Automation*.
47:- **Auto-send build and runtime errors** — Optionally send build errors (with warnings for context) to the active agent automatically whenever a Visual Studio build finishes with errors, so it can fix them. While debugging, unhandled exceptions can be sent the same way, with their stack trace. Opt-in via *⚙ → Settings... → Automation*.
59:- **Theme aware** — Follows VS dark/light theme automatically, or force dark, light, or a custom background color via *⚙ → Settings → Appearance*. Prompt zoom is persisted across sessions, and native chat zoom (Ctrl+Scroll, Ctrl+0 resets it) is too; set the terminal's console font and size via *⚙ → Settings → Terminal* (Ctrl+Scroll zoom applies for the current session).
61:- **20 languages support**: English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish, Korean, German, French, Russian, Traditional Chinese, Indonesian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Polish, Italian, Ukrainian, Arabic, Hindi, Thai and Dutch. Pick one under *⚙ → Settings → Appearance → Language*, or leave it on Automatic to follow the Visual Studio language.

## OpenPets

OpenPets MCP tools may be available.

Use OpenPets as a short visible status channel for meaningful coding progress:
- Use `openpets_say` when starting, completing, blocking, or needing review on non-trivial work.
- Keep messages brief, user-facing, and non-sensitive.
- Do not include code, logs, secrets, URLs, or file paths.
- Use `openpets_react` for small visual or emotional feedback.
- Use `openpets_status` only when checking availability or the targeted pet.
- Do not spam every internal step.

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke (dliedke@gmail.com) | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

---

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

---

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke (dliedke@gmail.com) | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

---

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.
